title: E-signature software compared
content_html:
An e-signature software comparison should start with your own documents, not with a feature list. Check which type of electronic signature your contracts need, who signs them, where signed files must end up and where the vendor stores your data. Then test two or three tools on a real contract before you commit.

Start with your process, not with a brand

Most teams compare e-signature tools by reading feature pages side by side. Those pages tend to look alike. The things that set tools apart are usually specific to your own work:

  • Who signs. Is it your own staff, your customers, your suppliers or all three?
  • What gets signed. Is it one standard contract, many versions of one template, or a different document every time?
  • Where the document comes from. Is it made by hand, or does it come from your CRM, ERP or a document folder?
  • Where the signed file goes. Does it need to land back in a customer record, an archive or a finance system?

Write these four answers down first. They tell you which questions matter for your shortlist.

How to run an e-signature software comparison

Put each tool on your shortlist through the same questions. Ask the vendor directly, and check its current website and terms. Do not rely on old reviews.

QuestionWhy it mattersHow to check
Which types of electronic signature does the tool support?Some documents need a stronger type of signature than others.Ask your legal adviser what your documents need, then ask the vendor which types it offers.
What does the signer have to do?External signers give up when a process feels hard.Send a test document to someone outside your company and watch them sign it.
What record does the tool keep of each signature?You may need to show later who signed, and when.Ask for an example of the record you get after signing.
Where is your data stored and processed?Contracts often hold personal data.Read the vendor's terms and ask for a processing agreement.
How does it connect to your other systems?A signed contract that someone has to save by hand is still manual work.Ask which systems it connects to, and test the connection you need.
Can it handle your language and your signers' language?Signers read the invite and the signing screen, not just the contract.Run a test in Dutch and in English if you need both.
How is it charged?Pricing models differ between vendors.Compare the price against your real volume of documents and users.

Test on a real contract, not a sample file. A real contract shows quickly where the tool fits your process and where it does not.

Where DocSign from Upward Technologies fits

Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) is a software company in Breda. Its e-signature product is called DocSign. DocSign is a separate product that is sold and used on its own. You do not need custom software or any other Upward product to use it.

Put DocSign on your shortlist next to the other tools you are looking at, and run it through the same questions in the table above. For a wider look at choosing a signing tool, see this guide on the best e-signature software.

Upward Technologies is also building ERIS, an all-in-one business system that runs on the client's own hardware with local AI. Its document signing module is in development for the beta, which starts in November 2026. ERIS is not available yet. It is a separate system and does not include DocSign.

When another tool is the better choice

Pick the tool that fits your process best, even if it is not DocSign:

  • A tool you already pay for offers signing. Check it first. One less tool means one less login and one less contract.
  • Your legal adviser says you need a signature type that a tool does not support. Leave that tool off your list.
  • Your signers already use a certain tool and are used to it. That can matter more than a small difference in features.

When signing is one step in a bigger process

Sometimes the problem is not the signature. The problem is everything around it: building the contract from customer data, chasing signers and filing the result. In that case, a signing tool on its own may not be enough.

Upward Technologies also builds custom software and integrations so data moves between systems without retyping. Every project starts with a three-week paid scoping phase before anything is built. It ends with a document the client could take to another supplier and a go or no-go decision. "Wrong supplier" can be the outcome. If you are weighing Upward Technologies against other builders, read this comparison of Upward Technologies and Dutch custom software agencies.

If signed files also need to be sent to people outside your company, this guide on choosing secure file transfer software covers that step.

How we compared

This page does not rank vendors on features. Vendor feature sets change, and this page only states facts that can be checked. It compares on what decides the fit for your team:

  • the signature types your documents need
  • the experience for the people who sign
  • the record kept after signing
  • where your data is stored and processed
  • the connections to the systems you already use
  • language support for your signers
  • how the price fits your real volume
